---
title: "Brand themes via `_brand.yml`"
---

## Overview

Quarto projects can be themed via three knobs that compose:

1. A built-in Bootswatch theme name (e.g. `cosmo`, `darkly`).
2. A `_brand.yml` file describing the project's colors, typography,
   and logo.
3. One or more custom `.scss` files with additional overrides.

The `theme:` array picks which of these contribute to the final CSS.
Their order controls precedence: later entries override earlier ones.

## A worked example

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: default
format:
  html:
    theme:
      - cosmo            # Bootswatch base
      - brand            # _brand.yml layer
      - extras.scss      # final user tweaks
brand: _brand.yml
```

```yaml
# _brand.yml
color:
  palette:
    brand-blue: "#0066cc"
  primary: brand-blue
  foreground: "#222"
typography:
  base:
    family: Georgia
```

This configuration renders with `cosmo` as the base palette, brand
colors and typography overlaid on top, and any rules from
`extras.scss` applied last.

## The `brand` token

The literal token `brand` in the `theme:` array is a **position
marker**. When the project also declares a `brand:` key, the marker
expands to the brand-derived SCSS layers at that exact position.

If you only set `brand:` (no `theme:`), Quarto auto-injects the
marker at the end — equivalent to writing `theme: [brand]`.

### `brand:` must be declared explicitly

Quarto 2 does **not** auto-discover `_brand.yml` from the project
root. If you want brand styling, you must declare the `brand:` key
in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
brand: _brand.yml
```

If `brand` appears in `theme:` without a corresponding `brand:` key,
the render fails with a clear configuration error rather than
silently shipping an unstyled page. This is deliberately stricter
than Quarto 1's auto-discovery: an explicit error pointing at the
missing configuration is more useful than a quietly broken render.

## `_brand.yml` shape

```yaml
color:
  palette:
    <name>: <css color>       # Named aliases. Emitted as $brand-<name>
                              # SCSS variables and --brand-<name> CSS
                              # custom properties.
  primary: <name or color>    # Bootstrap theme color slots. Values
  secondary: ...              # can reference palette entries.
  foreground: ...
  background: ...

typography:
  fonts:
    - source: google           # or bunny / file / system
      family: <name>
      weight: <number, array, or keyword>
      style: normal | italic | [normal, italic]
  base:                        # Body text settings
    family: <font name>
    size: <CSS length>
    weight: <number or keyword>
    line-height: <number>
  headings: { ... }            # Same shape as base
  link: { color, weight, decoration, ... }
  monospace: { ... }
  monospace-inline: { ... }    # Overrides monospace for inline code
  monospace-block: { ... }     # Overrides monospace for code blocks

logo:
  small: <path>                # Or { light, dark } for paired logos
  medium: <path>
  large: <path>
  images:                      # Named extra images
    <name>:
      path: <path>
      alt: <text>

defaults:
  bootstrap:
    defaults:                  # Map of $sass-var: value, applied
      font-size-base: 1.1rem   # before Bootstrap's own defaults
    uses: |                    # Free-form SCSS passthrough into the
      @use "sass:math";        # appropriate layer section
    rules: |
      .my-class { color: red; }
```

All sections are optional. A brand with just `color: { primary: red }`
is valid.

## Color resolution

Color references are resolved through a chain:

1. If the name is a palette key (`color.palette.<name>`), recurse on
   its value.
2. Else if the name is a theme color (`primary`, `secondary`,
   `foreground`, `background`, ...) and that slot is set, recurse on
   its value.
3. Else, treat the name as a raw CSS color and return it.

Aliases can chain (`primary: brand-blue` → `brand-blue: "#0066cc"`).
Cycles are detected and reported as errors.

## What CSS gets generated

From the worked example above, the compiled theme CSS contains, among
many other rules:

```css
/* From color.palette */
:root {
  --brand-brand-blue: #0066cc;
}

/* From the named theme colors and the format-specific name map */
$primary: #0066cc !default;
$foreground: #222 !default;
$body-color: #222 !default;    /* foreground → body-color */
$pre-color: #222 !default;     /* foreground → pre-color */

/* From typography.base */
$font-family-base: "Georgia" !default;
```

## What is **not** yet supported

- **Light/dark brand pairs** (`brand: { light: ..., dark: ... }`) —
  parsed but only the light half is used; tracked as a follow-up
  until Q2 grows a light/dark seam in the SCSS pipeline.
- **Inline brand block in document frontmatter** — only the
  project-level `brand:` key in `_quarto.yml` is supported for now.
- **Brand-aware favicon / navbar brand image** — the brand data is
  available, but the website pipeline doesn't yet read it. Tracked
  as separate follow-ups.
- **Typst `_brand.yml`** — HTML only for now.
